transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Petra 3 FP, Anselm 3 FP, Caddock 3 FP, Yarrow 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], The Pikemaw [T-05].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain hammers the plank walkways of Hollowmoot, and the water beneath them has crept up another rung of the pilings overnight. A woman named Ness shoves through the queue at the toll-shrine, soaked to the bone, and grabs whichever of you looks least likely to turn her away. Her boy Tam, she says, went out three nights ago chasing a sound only he could hear — the swarm-song — and hasn't come back. Everyone knows where that song comes from: the drowned belltower of Saint Orrin's temple, out past the reed channels where the Pikemaw hunts. Behind her, a Warden at the tollgate is already eyeing the party, counting how many mouths just arrived in his town and wondering what they'll cost him.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: I know that song—I've heard it calling since I was small. Your Tam didn't wander off foolish; he was called. And I swore an oath to ring everyone home before this flood takes them. Help me understand: when did the song start speaking his name?

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra's head tilts sharply at Ness's words, and her eyes go distant for just a moment—the look of someone listening to something no one else can hear. She steps toward the soaked woman with sudden certainty, reaching out to steady her. The rain drums on the walkway around them, and Petra's jaw sets with grim recognition. She's heard the swarm-song her whole life. She knows exactly what it does to people who aren't ready for it.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: Tell me everything about Tam. When did he leave, and what exactly did he hear?

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm holds Ness steady, his grip firm. This is the trail he's been hunting for—the bell-tongue of Saint Orrin, the swarm-song emanating from its drowned tower. His eyes lock onto hers with complete, undivided attention. Everything else—the Warden, the rain, the rising water—fades for this moment.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: How long has the boy been out? And when he left—did anyone see which way he went toward the temple?

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock steadies herself as Ness grabs for her, taking in the woman's drenched state and wild eyes. She places a calming hand on Ness's arm, her weathered midwife's grip sure and practiced.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Steady yourself — your boy's still out there, and we'll find him. I know these waters better than most; tell me exactly where he went and when you last heard that song.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow lowers his hand to meet Ness at eye level, his weathered face grave but determined. He's already calculating the routes through the reed channels and the tidal windows, his fingers absently checking that his gear is secure. Brack, sensing his intent, rises from where the hound has been resting, alert and ready.)

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: "I know what calls to him. When did Tam's name first sound in—" My voice dies as something vast answers, and I can't move.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ness's mouth is already forming an answer—"Three nights, past dusk, he just stopped and stared out past the pilings and said 'it's calling my—'"—when Petra's question cuts the air and something answers it. Not Ness. A low, vast drone rolls in from somewhere past the rooftops, felt in the teeth more than heard, and Petra goes rigid mid-word, eyes rolled half to white, one hand locked white-knuckled on the rail. Ness flinches back with a small cry; the Warden at the tollgate goes very still, hand drifting to the haft of his hook-pole, muttering "Saint's mercy, not another one" under his breath as he studies Petra like she might turn feral right there on the planks. The sound fades as quickly as it came, leaving the ordinary hiss of rain and the creak of rope — but everyone who heard it knows exactly which direction it came from: out past the reed channels, toward the drowned belltower.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: It's answering me. The song—it knows I'm here now, and it's answering. We don't have time anymore; we have to go after Tam before it pulls anyone else into the channels.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra's fingers slowly uncurl from the rail with a visible tremor. Her breath comes in ragged gasps as the paralysis releases her limbs one joint at a time, and she staggers back half a step, one hand pressed hard against her sternum as if she can feel the vast drone still vibrating through her ribs. Her eyes—still swimming back into focus—lock onto Ness with sudden, fierce clarity. She's been hearing the swarm-song her whole life, but she's never *answered* it, never called out to it directly. And it answered her. She swallows hard, tasting copper and rainwater, and her jaw tightens with the weight of her own oath. Before this morning, it was abstract—a voice in the reeds, a danger everyone whispered about. Now it's *present*. Now it knows her name too.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: Petra, stay with us—what did you hear?

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm pivots toward Petra, his hand finding her shoulder with steady pressure. His eyes search hers for signs of corruption or possession—the glassy stare, the subtle wrongness beneath the skin. Around them, Ness cowers and the Warden's grip tightens on his hook-pole, but Anselm remains calm, focused. The swarm-song did not simply emit a sound—it answered Petra's question. It understands language. It is hunting them as much as they hunt it.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Petra—you with us? The Warden here doesn't need to understand everything; we're looking for a lost boy, and I know the way through the reeds. Ness, go to the shrine and wait—we'll bring Tam back.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow moves to Petra's side to steady her if she needs it, his weathered hand firm on her shoulder. He turns to face the Warden with the calm, practiced authority of someone who once wore the militia colors—not challenging, just... certain. There's no question in his stance. Brack shifts to Yarrow's flank, hackles settled but ready. Without waiting for further argument, Yarrow starts moving toward the walkway that leads into the reed channels, trusting the others to follow. The marsh is where he holds the line.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: The oath holds, Warden—it's held this long and I've kept it. But I swore to Ness I'd find her boy, and now those two promises are pulling me in opposite directions. Tell me true: do I let Tam drown to keep the old word?

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Yarrow's old promise doesn't answer him — it just sits there, a stone in his gut, because Ness's tears are more real than any oath sworn to dead men. He makes his choice fast, before he can talk himself out of it: "The boy first. The rest of you can hold me to account after." Brack barks once, sharp, and noses toward the reed line as if he'd already decided the same thing. The Warden at the tollgate doesn't try to stop you — one look at Petra, still pale and trembling from whatever answered her, and he backs off a step, hook-pole lowered but not put away. "Go on, then," he mutters, "but if that girl comes back wrong, she doesn't come back into Hollowmoot." Ness presses a damp scrap of Tam's shirt into Caddock's hands — something for the boy to recognize, or something for you to track him by — and sinks down against the shrine post to wait, wringing her hands. Behind you, the walkways of Hollowmoot fall away into grey rain as the reed channels open ahead, the drowned belltower a smudge of dark stone somewhere past the current, and the Pikemaw's water waiting between here and there.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Brack's nose leads you off the plank walkways and into the reeds, where the safe pilings give way to black water and mats of drowned grass. The drone Petra heard hasn't stopped — if anything it's louder here, a hum you feel in your fillings, and half-sunk footprints stitch a line straight toward it before vanishing into a stretch of reed mat that looks solid and isn't. Somewhere out past the tree-line, something big enough to shiver the water disturbs a heron into flight. Ness stays behind at the tree line, wringing her hands, unwilling to go further and unable to leave.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: The song's got a shape to it—something's holding Tam in it like water in cupped hands. It's not just calling anymore, it's *keeping* him. We go careful, we go quiet, because whatever's out there is listening too.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra tilts her head, eyes half-closed, letting the drone wash over her entirely. Her whole body seems to tune itself to it—breathing synchronized with the pulse, fingers flexing as if conducting. Then her eyes snap open and she moves forward with slow, deliberate steps into the reeds, testing each mat of vegetation carefully before putting her weight on it. She holds up a hand to the others: *wait, watch me, follow my path*.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: The bell-tongue. After all this time, it's here. It's singing—and the boy heard it just like I did that night.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm stops abruptly in the reeds, raising a fist. The drone's vibration sharpens in his perception—he recognizes it from his studies and nightmares. He touches the blessed medallion at his neck, his hand trembling slightly as the pieces align.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: The boy went straight toward the sound, no meandering. This reed mat won't hold much longer—the water's already taking it back.

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock kneels by the footprints where Brack's trail goes cold, running a weathered hand over the torn reeds and soft ground. She traces each impression, feeling how the water is already welling back into them. Her eyes follow the path deeper into the reed mat, toward where the hum is loudest.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: One foot in front of the other. The boy's out here somewhere.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow moves forward along the barely-visible trail of half-sunk footprints, every step deliberate and testing the ground ahead. His eyes scan the water's surface and the reed mat, alert for movement from below and soft spots that might swallow a man whole. Brack stays at his heels, nose working.)

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: I know it—I *know* when something hears you back.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Anselm — create advantage with Lore: dice 0 0 0 0 → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — overcome with Notice: dice + 0 0 0 → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The vibration sharpens in Anselm's mind like a struck bell finally coming into tune—he names it aloud, "The bell-tongue... it's not just ringing, it's *singing itself hoarse*, over and over," and the words seem to peel back the reeds themselves, making the drone's true direction unmistakable to everyone at once. Yarrow doesn't hesitate; he reads the half-sunk footprints, the bent grass, the faint smear of a boy's palm on a fallen post, and finds a hard, dry line of old pilings threading clean through the mire exactly where the black water looks safest and isn't. Brack surges ahead along it without a single false step. Within minutes the reed screen breaks open before you—and there it is: Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple, its nave sunk to the eaves, its belltower alone still standing dry above the flood, the drone rolling out of its dark windows like a held breath. Ness's boy went this way. So, now, do you.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The reeds thin and drop away, and the temple rises out of the black water like a half-swallowed skull — nave flooded to the windowsills, roof caved in, the belltower jutting above the flood the only thing still dry. The drone is a scream now, up close, a single bell-note wrenched over and over until it cracks and starts again. Wading shapes move in the flooded nave below the tower — pale, slow, patient, drawn same as Tam was — and one of them turns toward the sound of your approach with water sheeting off its shoulders. Somewhere above, faint and human, a boy's voice is sobbing in time with the bell.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: Tam! I hear you! Hold on—I'm coming up!

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra wades into the flooded nave, her sharp ears straining to untangle the screaming bell from Tam's sobs, from the swarm-song that thrums in her teeth and tries to pull her under its spell. She forces her feet forward, mapping every sound—the bell's fractured rhythm, the soft splashing of pale shapes in the water, the exact position of the tower above. The song wants her to freeze, but her vow is stronger.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: Whether or not you have a soul left in there, you're not taking the boy. Not while I'm breathing.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm wades forward into the black water to intercept the creature that turned toward them. His hand goes to his weapon, movements sharp and practiced—the grim certainty of an exorcist who knows what needs to be done, even if he remains unsure what he's actually fighting.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Behind me! This one doesn't get past!

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow surges forward through the black water, not giving the creature time to advance further. He plants himself squarely between the pale, wading thing and his companions, fists clenched and ready. Brack barks sharply and moves with him, bristles raised, ready to fight.)

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: No—no, I know where you are, I can— *[her voice catches, going thin and strange]* —why does it sound like—

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — overcome with Notice: dice - 0 + + → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Anselm — attack with Fight: dice - - 0 0, invoking Hunting the Silenced Bell-Tongue of Saint Orrin [AN-A3] → Fair (+2) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS (Hive-Touched Pilgrim stress 1)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — attack with Fight: dice 0 0 0 0, invoking Disgraced Militia Guard Who Still Holds the Line [YA-HC], Bonded to Brack, the Marsh Hound [YA-A2] → Superb (+5) vs Fantastic (+6): SUCCESS MAJOR COST (Hive-Touched Pilgrim stress 2)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Yarrow's fist connects hard enough to stagger the pilgrim back into the flooded pews — but his own follow-through carries him too far. His boot finds no floor, just a sudden drop where the nave's stones have given way, and he plunges chest-deep into black water, the cold punching the air from his lungs. His knife spins from numb fingers into the dark, and for one long breath he can't find the bottom at all — Brack barking frantically at the water's edge, unable to follow.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text:
Petra's straining focus snaps everything into place at once — she has it now, the exact rhythm of the bell, the precise seam between Tam's sobs and the swarm's drone, and the fastest dry line up into the tower. She calls it out, sharp and certain, and for the first time since you waded in, the way forward is clear. Meanwhile Anselm's blade opens a shallow line across the first pilgrim's shoulder — it barely flinches, pain-blind, but staggers half a step. Yarrow's punch is the one that matters: it drives the creature reeling back into the broken pews, stunned — but Yarrow's own momentum betrays him. The nave floor simply isn't there anymore where he expects it, and he goes under, cold water closing over his head, his knife lost to the dark, Brack howling uselessly at the edge of a drop-off he can't cross.

The second pale shape in the water hasn't moved yet — but it's turning now, drawn by the splashing and the dog's bark, wading toward where Yarrow went down.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: I hear you—every sound you make, I hear it! I've got you!

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra's attention snaps from the tower to Yarrow in a heartbeat. She knows exactly where he is—she can hear every splash, every desperate gasp, the exact position of the pilgrim wading toward him. She drives forward into the black water with absolute certainty, her feet finding purchase on broken nave stones that should be hidden, navigating by sound alone as she moves to reach Yarrow before the creature does.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: Not again—I will not watch another drown!

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Yarrow goes under and Anselm's world narrows to one moment—the black water of the Drowned Mill, his sister's cry, that old horror made present. He turns hard from the first pilgrim, wading toward the second creature moving on Yarrow. He invokes that deep, terrible weight of survival—Survivor of the Drowned Mill, Haunted by His Sister's Cry—raising his blade to strike before this thing can drag Yarrow deeper.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: I've got you—hold on.

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock splashes forward into the black water without hesitation, her strong frame moving with the practiced ease of someone who knows these marshes. She wades toward where Yarrow went under, hands reaching through the cold dark.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Not going down—not here!

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow thrashes upward through the black water, refusing to go under. His numbed limbs burn as they fight the cold and the drag of stone; he claws desperately for air and light and solid ground. Brack's frantic barking above calls to him like a rope, and Yarrow surges toward it with stubborn animal desperation—refusing to yield, refusing to let that second pilgrim advance toward his friends while he still draws breath.)

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: No—no, no no no—*move*—why won't you—

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — overcome with Notice: dice - 0 + -, invoking Vowed to Ring Everyone Home Before the Flood [PE-A2] → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Anselm — attack with Fight: dice 0 0 + -, invoking Survivor of the Drowned Mill, Haunted by His Sister's Cry [AN-A1] → Great (+4) vs Great (+4): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Caddock — overcome with Physique: dice + + - - → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — overcome with Physique: dice + - 0 + → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Anselm's blade bites into the second pilgrim, staggering it back—but it lashes out as it falls, blunt fingers raking his forearm hard enough to numb it, and his sister's cry rings loud in his ears, drowning his focus for a breath.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Yarrow breaks the surface with a ragged gasp just as Caddock's hands close on his collar, hauling him up onto a submerged step before the cold can claim him again—soaked, shaking, but breathing. Petra reaches them in the same instant, having read the water perfectly; she plants herself at Yarrow's side, eyes still fixed upward on the tower, refusing to let the swarm-song pull her attention away again. Anselm's blade catches the second pilgrim across the ribs, doubling it over—but as it falls it snags his sleeve, and for one terrible heartbeat he's back at the Drowned Mill, his sister's cry drowning out the fight around him; he shakes it off just in time to see the creature isn't done yet, staggered but still coming. Above you all, the bell shrieks on, and Tam's sobbing breaks into a wordless, keening wail—whatever's happening up there, it's getting worse.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: Tam! I hear you—I'm coming for you, hold on!

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra reads the water and the pilgrim's movement like a map written in sound. She finds the gap, threads it, and pushes toward the tower stairs—leaving Anselm and Yarrow to hold the remaining threat behind her. The swarm-song shrieks and pulls, but her vow burns brighter than the compulsion to freeze. She's moving. She's coming.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: You won't have him. Not while I draw breath.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm plants himself firmly between the creature and Yarrow, blade steady despite the burn of the rake across his forearm. That terror when Yarrow went under—it pulled his sister's cry out of the past and into the black water before him, alive and present. This thing will not drag another soul down into that darkness. He attacks with sharp, controlled purpose, the focused will of an exorcist who knows exactly what must be done.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: Not getting past us.

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock steps forward and wraps her strong arms around the pale creature's shoulders, pinning its arms to its body while Anselm presses his blade.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: You don't get past me. Not now, not ever.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow surges up from the black water in a fighting crouch, drawing on everything that's made him hold the line through all his failures—Disgraced Militia Guard Who Still Holds the Line. Brack snarls at his shoulder, their bond unbreakable—Bonded to Brack, the Marsh Hound. Together they plant themselves squarely between the advancing pilgrim and their companions, fists raised despite the cold and the numbness, refusing to yield, refusing to break.)

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: *[Her name—her own name, woven into the drone, pulling at something that lives below her skin]* No—no, I—*[her voice breaks into something not quite human, a keening that mirrors the bell]*

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: Don't waste time on me! Keep that thing pinned!

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Anselm accepts a compel.

transcript.text: Petra — overcome with Notice: dice + + + + → Legendary (+8) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Anselm — attack with Fight: dice + + + - → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Hive-Touched Pilgrim (second) mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Caddock — attack with Physique: dice - 0 0 + → Great (+4) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Hive-Touched Pilgrim (second) taken out)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — attack with Fight: dice 0 0 + -, invoking Disgraced Militia Guard Who Still Holds the Line [YA-HC], Bonded to Brack, the Marsh Hound [YA-A2] → Superb (+5) vs Poor (-1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Hive-Touched Pilgrim (second) taken out)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The second pilgrim goes down hard, first buckling under Anselm's blade and Caddock's crushing grip, then driven fully under by Yarrow's last desperate punch—it stops moving, sinking to its knees in the flooded pews and staying there. The first pilgrim, staggered and bleeding, doesn't press the fight; it only stands swaying in the shallows, watching, as if the bell above has already forgotten it. Petra doesn't look back. She's already at the tower stairs, water sheeting off her boots, climbing toward the sound of Tam's wail with her vow ringing louder in her than any swarm-song. Behind her the nave goes quiet but for the drip of water and Brack's low, wary growl—and above, the cracked bell tolls once more, and Tam's voice breaks into something that isn't quite crying anymore.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The stair up is drowned rope and broken stone, but it climbs, and Petra's certainty about the rhythm carries you past the worst of it into a tower that's somehow still dry. Up here the drone isn't distant anymore — it comes from the great bronze bell itself, and from the boy huddled beneath it, one small hand pressed flat to the metal like he's trying to feel a heartbeat through it. Tam doesn't turn around. His lips move with the bell's groan, perfectly in time, and where his fingers touch bronze the metal weeps a thin black sheen that isn't rust. Below, through the shattered belfry slats, the first pilgrim you left standing in the shallows has started, slowly, to wade toward the stairs.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: Tam, let go. I hear it—I hear exactly what you hear. But you don't have to carry it alone anymore. Let me take it from here.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra moves toward Tam, her eyes fixed on him and the weeping black sheen where his fingers touch the bronze. She has found the rhythm now—the precise seam between his sobs and the swarm's drone that she grasped on the climb up. The song has him caught, but she hears it as clearly as he does. She reaches for him with her hand open, speaking with the quiet certainty of her vow burning behind every word, her understanding of the song making her the only one in this tower who might reach him.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: Whatever that bell is telling you, the answer is no. And whoever's coming up those stairs, they don't get past me.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm steps forward to stand between Tam and the stairs descending to the flooded temple below. His eyes remain fixed on the boy, recognizing the bell-tongue artifact—the very thing he's been hunting—and understanding now exactly how it feeds: through living voices, through amplification, through a child's cry. His hand drops to his blade as the sound of the pilgrim's slow, deliberate climb echoes from below.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: I won't let you through.

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock moves to the top of the stairs and plants herself firmly in the doorway, using her full strength and bulk to create an absolute barrier between the pilgrim and the boy.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: Tam! Come on, lad—your mother sent me for you. We're going NOW!

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow strides to Tam in three quick steps and grabs him by both shoulders, putting all his soaked and aching strength into physically pulling the boy away from the bell and that weeping black sheen.)

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: No—no, I hear you, I hear—

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — overcome with Notice: dice 0 + - - → Good (+3) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Caddock — overcome with Physique: dice 0 0 + - → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — overcome with Physique: dice + - + 0 → Great (+4) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Yarrow's grip closes on Tam's shoulders and hauls, and for one terrible second the boy's fingers seem to fuse to the bronze — then they tear free with a wet, sucking snap, the black sheen whipping back into the bell like a struck cord. Tam gasps, blinking, suddenly a child again instead of a metronome, and collapses backward into Yarrow's soaked arms, sobbing his mother's name instead of the swarm's rhythm. Petra reaches out at the same instant, and for one heartbeat the song calls her name too — she freezes mid-step, eyes glazing, caught by the very trouble she carries — but she'd already found the seam in the rhythm on the climb up, and even frozen she starts humming it back, off-key and human, cutting cleanly against the drone until it staggers and breaks like a voice losing its pitch. The great bell shudders, its groan fracturing into something smaller, almost apologetic, as if it's lost its grip on the room. Below, the first pilgrim reaches the stairs — and finds Caddock filling the doorway like a wall of wet stone, immovable, arms braced against the frame; it claws once at her shoulder, finds nothing to grab past her bulk, and slumps back down a step, confused and swaying, its purpose momentarily unmoored now that the bell itself has gone quiet. In the sudden hush, rain drums on the belfry slats and Tam's crying is the only sound left that means anything.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Tam's breathing steadies against Yarrow's shoulder, but below, through the broken belltower floor, you all hear it — not the drone this time, but splashing. Many feet, moving with purpose now instead of the slow drift of the hive-touched. The bell above you is silent for the first time in three nights, and that silence seems to have woken something. Through the tower's shattered window, the black water outside is visibly higher than when you waded in, swallowing the last dry stones of the stair you climbed. Getting Tam — and yourselves — back out is no longer just a matter of retracing your steps.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: There—the bell-keeper's passage. We don't go down. We go up through the bell frame and across the roof struts to the far side of the nave. It's going to be terrifying and slippery, but it gets us away from whatever is moving through that floodwater.

transcript.speaker: Petra
transcript.text: (Petra closes her eyes for one breath, reading the tower through vibration and touch—the water's rise, the timber's voice, the bell's shadow on everything. Her apprenticeship taught her that bell-keepers build escape routes into their sanctuaries. She moves with sudden certainty, hands finding the maintenance hatch behind the bell's frame, the rope ladder coiled there for emergencies. Above us is not safety, but it's not drowning either.)

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: The water's taken the stair. They're coming up from below—moving with clear purpose now, not the slow drift of the hive-touched.

transcript.speaker: Anselm
transcript.text: (Anselm moves quickly to the broken window, blade drawn, eyes tracking the movements in the flooded temple below. The black water rises relentlessly, swallowing the last dry stones. He takes position between the tower stairs and where Yarrow shelters Tam, braced and ready for what's coming.)

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: We climb. Higher ground first.

transcript.speaker: Caddock
transcript.text: (Caddock quickly scans the tower, assessing where the water has reached and where higher ground still exists. She's worked in marshes and floods her whole life—she knows how water moves and finds the gaps it hasn't filled yet. She points upward with a sharp gesture.)

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: They're coming hard and fast. The water's nearly swallowed the stairs—if we're going down, it has to be now.

transcript.speaker: Yarrow
transcript.text: (Yarrow's jaw tightens as he listens to the splashing below, mentally cataloging every sound—the pace, the weight distribution, the rhythm of urgency in their movements. His militia training hasn't left him; he can read a threat in footsteps like others read the marsh. He shifts Tam higher on his hip, positioning himself at the edge of the broken floor to scan the dark water below while keeping the boy shielded against his shoulder. Brack presses close to his leg, hackles raised.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Petra — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 0 0 + → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Caddock — overcome with Notice: dice - 0 + 0, invoking Swamp Midwife Who Delivers in Any Weather [CA-HC] → Great (+4) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Yarrow — overcome with Notice: dice + + + - → Fantastic (+6) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Petra's instincts prove true — the hatch behind the bell's frame swings open on a rope ladder that's clearly been maintained for exactly this kind of emergency, coiled and ready as if some long-dead bell-keeper knew this night would come. Caddock reads the timber and water in an instant, calling the driest line across the struts before anyone else even sees it. Yarrow, Tam braced tight against his shoulder, doesn't waste the opening — he's first up through the hatch, Brack scrambling after with claws skittering on wet bronze, and his read of the sounds below tells him exactly how much time they've bought: not much, but enough. Below, the splashing surges up the drowned stair just as the last of you clears the hatch, and clawed, dripping hands slap against stone that's already empty. The party comes out onto the roof struts into open rain and grey light, the temple's shattered dome behind them, the flooded nave and its hunters falling away below — Tam alive and breathing, the bell silent, the way down cut off behind you instead of ahead.

Her whole body locks mid-step, foot hovering over the reed mat, eyes wide and unseeing, leaving the other

costs.tag: Freezes When the Song Calls Her Name
costs.text: As Petra strains to place the bell-tongue's rhythm, the swarm-song shifts and finds a shape almost like her own name buried in the drone. Her feet lock mid-step in the black water, the sound coiling tighter around her thoughts, costing her the moment she needed to keep mapping the nave.

Yarrow's fist connects hard enough to stagger the pilgrim back into the flooded pews — but his own follow-through carries him too far. His boot finds no floor, just a sudden drop where the nave's stones have given way, and he plunges chest-deep into black water, the cold punching the air from his lu

costs.tag: Freezes When the Song Calls Her Name
costs.text: As Petra drives through the black water toward Yarrow, the swarm-song swells and twists—for one heartbeat it sounds like her own name in the drone, and her feet lock mid-stride, the black water rising past her waist while she fights to move at all.

Anselm's blade bites into the second pilgrim, staggering it back—but it lashes out as it falls, blunt fingers raking his forearm hard enough to numb it, and his sister's cry rings loud in his ears, drowning his focus for a breath.

As she closes on the tower stairs, the swarm-song shifts—and inside it, unmistakably, her own name. Her feet lock mid-stride, the sound driving straight through her vow, and for a beat she cannot move at all.

The rake across his forearm is deeper than he let on—blood threading down into the black water—but when Caddock reaches for it he wrenches his arm away, snapping that it's nothing, and keeps his blade up despite the numbness spreading toward his fingers.

costs.tag: Freezes When the Song Calls Her Name
costs.text: As Petra opens herself to the song's rhythm to reach Tam, the drone shifts and croons her own name back at her in Tam's cracked voice — and for one terrible beat her outstretched hand stops dead, fingers trembling an inch from his shoulder.

Tie on an attack: 'success at minor cost' but 0 shifts of harm.

ambiguities.issue: The rules say a tie is 'success at a minor cost' and a fail may be taken as 'success at a major cost', with 'the GM invents costs,' but never specify whether such a cost must manifest as mechanical stress/consequence damage or can be purely narrative. In the log, the major cost at event 41-42 (Yarrow falling through the floor into black water) and the minor cost at event 49-52 (Anselm's numbed arm/distraction) were both resolved as pure narration with no stress-track or consequence entries logged anywhere in the session.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated all success-at-a-cost outcomes as purely narrative complications; no stress boxes or consequence slots were marked for these costs.

ambiguities.issue: The same apparent trouble aspect for Petra is referenced under two different tag identifiers across the log: the full phrase 'Freezes When the Song Calls Her Name' (events 10, 24, 38, 47, 70) and the short code 'PE-TR' (event 57), with near-identical fictional text. The rules do not define how trouble aspects should be tagged/identified consistently for compel bookkeeping.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated 'PE-TR' and 'Freezes When the Song Calls Her Name' as the same aspect and paid the standard +1 fate point compel award.

ambiguities.issue: The rules state the GM 'may offer a compel on any player aspect or trouble whenever the story calls for it' but set no cap on how often the same aspect can be compelled within a single scene. Scene 3 alone saw Petra's trouble aspect compelled three separate times (events 38, 47, 57), each paying a fresh fate point.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: All three same-scene compels on the same aspect were accepted and each paid out 1 fate point, with no reduction or scene-level cap applied.

The same trouble aspect is tracked under two different tag spellings ('Freezes When the Song Calls Her Name' vs 'PE-TR'), which could cause downstream bookkeeping/engine matching errors if the two are ever treated as distinct aspects.

free_text.best_moment: When Petra hummed off-key to shatter the bell's hold on her—the moment she used her core ability (hearing the swarm-song) to overcome her core trouble (freezing when it calls her name). It felt like a triumph of character defiance rather than just luck or outside help.
free_text.most_frustrating: The repeated compels on my trouble left Petra paralyzed multiple times, especially when the song called her name right as she was trying to save Tam. That helplessness was intense—though I recognize it was dramatically earned and ultimately satisfying, not unfair.
free_text.background_used: Yes, extensively and well. The bell-ringer apprenticeship wasn't just flavor—knowing the escape routes saved the party, understanding bell-tone and rhythm was mechanically essential, and the vow to "ring everyone home" was directly invoked and felt materially important to the story. Good integration.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to learn more about or confront the Dry Saint (my marked enemy) or understand what the swarm-song actually *wants*. The urgency and danger didn't allow for deeper investigation, which is probably right for the pacing but left that thread dangling.
free_text.one_sentence: My bell-ringer apprenticeship was used expertly—it gave me specific knowledge and abilities that made Petra essential to solving the crisis, giving real mechanical weight to the narrative.

free_text.best_moment: When Yarrow went under and my sister's cry came flooding back—the compel made my PTSD feel visceral and real rather than just mechanical. GM played my trauma perfectly.
free_text.most_frustrating: The bell-tongue mystery remains unsolved. I'm an exorcist uncertain if the hive has souls, and we silenced the bell and rescued Tam, but I still don't know what it *is* or how to truly stop it. Good hook, but unsatisfying.
free_text.background_used: good — The Drowned Mill trauma and the bell-tongue hunt were both woven in seamlessly, not forced. My backstory made my choices and reactions carry more weight.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: A chance to study the bell-tongue artifact directly with Lore, to investigate the black sheen and interrogate whether it has consciousness. Combat moved too fast for deliberate investigation.
free_text.one_sentence: My backstory was used well—the bell-tongue hunt and the Drowned Mill trauma were organic to every scene and made me feel like a character with real stakes, not just a passenger.

free_text.best_moment: When I hauled Yarrow from the black water with a grip born from years of delivering people safely through dangerous conditions—then stood immovable in the tower doorway like "wet stone." Those moments made it clear that Caddock's strength and steadiness meant something when it mattered most.
free_text.most_frustrating: None of Caddock's specific history came into play. Marrowreed Village, Sella, the Wardens, the Cellars—all of it incidental. The story felt like it could have happened to any character with swamp-adjacent skills. I wanted the hive-touched pilgrims to matter *personally* to Caddock, not just tactically.
free_text.background_used: Partially; surface-level. The setting and scenario suited my profession well—marshland, rescue mission, physical endurance—but my actual relationships and history were never engaged. The fit was thematic but not personal.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More mechanical opportunities to invoke my aspects for bonuses (my trouble aspect never created a complication), and narrative space for Caddock's history to matter—something about Sella in those pilgrims, or the Wardens' shadow over this place, or even just a reason to care beyond "there's a boy to save."
free_text.one_sentence: My character concept fit the adventure perfectly, but my backstory felt incidental rather than woven in—I was the right skill set for the wrong reasons.

free_text.best_moment: When Yarrow went under in the flooded nave and clawed his way back up through the black water — it made him genuinely hold the line against drowning itself, and Brack's frantic barking was the rope that pulled him back to air.
free_text.most_frustrating: Wanted one concrete detail about the oath he broke — just a name, a face, a ghost of a reason — so the choice would hit even harder.
free_text.background_used: Yes. The compel on his trouble aspect felt organic and created real tension. Militia expertise, weir-keeper skills, and Brack's bond all got mechanical use. The oath breaking became a character-defining choice. Good.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Have a bigger role in investigating the swarm-song mystery — that felt like Petra's domain, and I wanted more detective work where Yarrow's Notice and background mattered.
free_text.one_sentence: Yarrow's backstory felt used as a genuine engine for character tension and meaningful moral choice, not just flavor text.

chronicle.summary: The party followed a swarm-song into Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple, fought back the hive-touched pilgrims through the flooded nave, and Yarrow tore Tam free of the bronze bell's hold just as the tower fell silent. As newly purposeful hive-touched surged up the drowned stair, Petra's instinct for the bell-keeper's hidden escape route got the party — and the rescued boy — out across the roof struts and away, leaving their hunters clawing at empty stone below. Hollowmoot's flood keeps rising, the bell is quiet for now, but something down in that temple learned to move with purpose tonight.
